title: Greater than, less than and equal signs
examples: What does the greater than sign mean?
How do I remember which sign is which?

left.ask: What does the greater than sign mean?

explain.say: Which is more: 8 sweets or 5 sweets? Imagine putting them on a seesaw. Look at the board: 8 on the left and 5 on the right. The 8 side goes down, because 8 is greater.

draw.text: Greater than, less than and equal signs

left.ask: What does the greater than sign mean?

explain.say: We write 8, then the greater than sign, then 5, and say 8 is greater than 5. The sign looks like a hungry crocodile mouth: it always opens towards the bigger number. Can you see the heavier side?

left.ask: What does the greater than sign mean?

explain.say: Now 3 on the left and 7 on the right. The 7 side goes down, so 3 is less than 7. In the less than sign, the small pointy end points at the smaller number. Which side is lighter?

left.ask: What does the less than sign mean?

explain.say: Here are 6 and 6. The seesaw is level! Equal amounts balance, so we use the equals sign: 6 equals 6. What could you put with 4 to make the other side level?

left.ask: What does the equals sign mean?

explain.say: Brilliant! Now 9 on one side, and 4 plus 4 on the other. 4 and 4 make 8, and 8 is less than 9, so the 9 side still wins. Wow: these signs were first printed in 1631, in a book by Thomas Harriot! Challenge: is 15 greater or less than 51?

faq.q: What does the greater than sign mean?
faq.a: The greater than sign shows that the first number is bigger. When you write 8 greater than 5, the open end faces the 8.

faq.q: What does the less than sign mean?
faq.a: The less than sign shows that the first number is smaller. When you write 3 less than 7, the small pointed end is at the 3.

faq.q: What does the equals sign mean?
faq.a: The equals sign means both sides are worth exactly the same, like a level seesaw. 6 equals 6, and 4 plus 2 equals 6 too.

faq.q: How do I remember which sign is which?
faq.a: Think of a hungry crocodile: its open mouth always faces the bigger number, because it wants to eat more. The pointy end faces the smaller number.
asks: How do I tell the signs apart?

faq.a: No. 51 has 5 tens and 15 has only 1 ten, so 51 is greater. 15 is less than 51.

facts: The greater than and less than signs were first printed in 1631, in a book by the English mathematician Thomas Harriot.
The equals sign was invented by Robert Recorde of Wales in 1557.

quiz.why: 9 is bigger than 4, so 9 is greater than 4.

wrong.1: 4 is smaller, so it cannot be greater than 9.
wrong.2: 9 and 4 are not the same amount.

quiz.say: Is 23 less than, greater than or equal to 32?
quiz.why: 23 has 2 tens and 32 has 3 tens, so 23 is less than 32.

wrong.2: 23 and 32 use the same digits but are not equal.
